reviewTextVerbatim:
**Result: keep DP04A as a preliminary salvage part only.** It is not visually approved and not ready for close-up use. The one correction I'd support is shortening the rear trim tip, which is optional. If the part has to hold up at isolated or close-up scale, I'd reject it and rebuild from the clean P04.

## What the images show

**Standalone part (1000 px, all six views; 256/128 left and rear three-quarter)**
- **Hole:** an irregular, roughly octagonal opening, about 0.27 × 0.22 m judging by pixel spans against the 0.83 × 0.67 m bounds. The dark fracture wall around it is the same thickness all the way round. It reads as a clean punched or cut opening, not torn metal. The rim has no ragged or thinned edges.
- **Damage area:** this is the biggest problem. All the folds sit inside a sharp, axis-aligned rectangle, roughly 0.55 × 0.32 m, visible on both the outer (left) and inner (right) faces. That makes the damage look like a manufactured inset bezel or pocket rather than physical disruption.
- **Folds:** they are broad, flat facets with knife-edge ridges. The front and top end views show them standing about 4–5 cm proud of the slab on one face. Long thin triangles run from the damage rectangle to the panel corners, most clearly the lower one running to the rear-lower corner. **Yes, they read as too sharp and exaggerated** when the part is seen on its own. The bulk of the relief seems to be on the outer face, so the folds look like they flare outward. I can't confirm that direction from the images alone, and I'm not treating it as a defect.
- **Rear trim tip: confirmed.** The rear seam strip hangs about 35–40 px (roughly 3.5 cm) below the raised rear-lower corner. You can see it in the left, right and rear three-quarter views. On its own the part looks like it has a loose stalk. This matches the record: corner vertices 25 and 29 were raised from Z 0.700 to 0.735 while the trim was kept exactly as it was. The front end is flush.
- **Dark streaks behind the hole:** soft streaks trail rearward in the standalone PBR views. They could be shadows cast by the folds or the `DP04A_Scuff` texture. I can't tell which from these renders.

**Assembled core (all six 256 views, left 1000/128, both three-quarter views at 1000)**
- At 1000 left, the damaged panel (the fourth skirt panel) looks the same as the D01 donor's 1000 left view, and the clean source shows no hole there. The rear-trim gap and the rectangular boundary can't be seen at this scale.
- At 256 the damage is a dark blob with a small flap. At 128 it is a speck.
- I don't attribute anything seen through the opening to DP04A, and I see nothing that suggests the Hull is penetrated.

**Scale:** the sharp folds, the rectangle and the trim tip only matter at part scale or close range. At whole-tank runtime sizes they disappear, which is why keeping it as a preliminary salvage part is defensible.

## Strongest objections
1. **The rectangular damage boundary.** This is the deciding visual flaw. It makes the damage look manufactured, and fixing it would mean designing new damage, which is outside a salvage recipe.
2. **Faceted folds with long corner-to-corner slivers.** The breach looks stylized and too big at part scale.
3. **The rear trim tip below the bent corner.** It's inherited, but it's real and visible.

## Supported correction (optional)
Shorten the lower end of the rear seam trim so it meets the inherited displaced corner at about Z 0.735. This only lines up existing trim with an existing corner and adds no new damage shape. It would still be a new authored revision that needs its own review. Fixing the rectangle or the folds would not be salvage. That would be the clean P04 rebuild route, keeping all the salvage history.

## What the technical records say (not verified by me)
These come from the producer's own records:
- 132 triangles, one mesh, 57 identity EMPTY frames.
- Validation passed with no issues.
- 18 standalone dimension criteria and 16 core criteria passed.
- Corner normals, UVs and PBR reported exact.
- In the core, the other 278 meshes are reported exact.

A technical pass doesn't make the visuals acceptable.

## Still outstanding
- I couldn't recompute any image or GLB hashes; I had no shell this session.
- `standalone-status.json` is too large (392 KB) to read, so I didn't read it. I read only the first 2,251 of 3,366 lines of `standalone-render.json`.
- The producer's own standalone render is framed at whole-vehicle scale, so the part is about 70 px across in it. Only the supplementary PBR images give part-scale evidence.
- The export lists 5 materials, including `DP04A_Scuff` but no "paint". The plan counts paint faces and validation reports 6 materials. I haven't checked how these names map to each other.

No producer or approval tools were used. Nothing here is a human score, approval, or user choice.
qualification: Independent agent review; no human approval or formal grade.
